column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; lead evidence that Taiwan's main private old-building grant asked no money proof at application (programme closed June 2022), so a custodian statement is more than asked.
Mon 16 Nov: store; Taipei judges track record and a reasonable budget, not a balance; written for running venues, so a new residency fits it poorly.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; city-owned buildings lent free, so the founder's share is never tested; serves no part.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; the split budget table is the Taiwanese form of 'here is my share', declared not proved; small grants.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 6 (own funding planned and scored, not proved); for city and county venues, not private founders.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; self-funding is scored as a ratio written in the budget, not proved; private bodies capped at NT$2m a year.
Mon 16 Nov: store; NCAF weighs finances in the round with no ratio or proof; read in part, so S 4.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the bankbook copy's purpose is not stated, so never cite it as proof of funds.

Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q11d-002 and Q11e-016 (the state's grant can be cut by a budget vote); the Taichung rule adds nothing new.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; the matching share is named in the contract papers, the Taiwanese stage where her figure would appear; 2023 text via a county repost.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; checks before money are on the building and the contract, not the owner's bank.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d; head row for claim 2: Taiwan proves an owner's share by receipts and a cost-split table at each instalment, never by a balance before.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 16 (own-funded work tracked and paid on actual spending at the agreed split); 2016 text.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 16 in the regional-revival grant (the share shown as a ratio of money spent).
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 16 (own share reported, not pre-proved); creative businesses, not residencies.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b beside card Q11e's founder-first order: in several rules the owner spends before the state pays; always 'several rules', since row 23 shows Taipei pays ahead; 2018 rule.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 20 (small grants reimburse after the owner spends); the MoC's national version, amendment date not shown.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the central-local rule bars spending a grant ahead of the matching share, but it binds governments, not private founders.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the qualifier row 20 needs: Taipei pays 70% within ten days, so 'the founder pays first' on timing is not universal.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d; a public co-funder proves committed money by a budget vote that a later vote can cut, Laura by ownership; a fair comparison, not a boast (Q30-033 has the vote, not the proof form).

Mon 16 Nov: 3d; Taipei's grant falls pro rata if the matching money spent falls short (Q11c-024 is the NEA's version); reword the use: never 'one-for-one grant', since SKELETON 3d says a Taiwanese funder never matches her money; public art, not buildings.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 25 (grant recalculated at the original ratio when spending falls), at the MoC, Taichung and Hsinchu.
Mon 16 Nov: store; adds that the owner's own spending is checked at unit prices, so in-kind shares may count; 2018 rule.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as Q9c-006 (unspent grant money returned in proportion).
Mon 16 Nov: store; clawback is for breach (false papers, misuse), not a shortfall, which only shrinks the grant; claim 4.
Mon 16 Nov: the bans are the consequence chain of row 29's clawback; Q10d-003 has the village grant's two-year bar.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as Q22-012 (every funder disclosed; concealment revokes the grant), here in four more rules.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b store; city grants of NT$0.5m-1.5m against her range; NT$3.11m is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS (only NT$3.77m is, 8j): label it at the 6 Nov rate or add it to NUMBERS; caps change yearly.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a warning to quote a Taiwanese ratio only from a clear text; the slip's meaning is Keel's reading.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3d store; a 20% own-funds floor for running costs is common; never say her ten payments qualify the residency for any grant (SKELETON 3d).
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as Q11e-016 (priority to owners with higher matching money), at three cities with a 70% line.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; designated-heritage owners' share fell from 10% to 5%: the state's share is policy; heritage, not Laura's case.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; general arts money will not pay for walls, which supports the ask's two parts (capital, and yearly programme money).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; founding a foundation proves endowed property once; Taiwan legal form is out of scope.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; the one proof form found is a Taiwan-dollar time deposit; say her Treasuries pay out and are converted, never 'sold' (IPS l.13, held to the end); sample charter, not law.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; dedicated accounts and 100% cash are foundation-capital rules, not grant rules; Taiwan legal is out of scope.
Mon 16 Nov: store; Taiwan's Foundations Act lets foundation capital buy government bonds, the same instinct as the ladder; never claim US Treasuries qualify (UNVERIFIED).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; concession tenders examine a balance sheet up front, a different deal from a co-sponsored residency.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; Taiwanese contracts take Taiwanese government bonds as security; foreign bonds not stated, so no parallel claim.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d guard; UNVERIFIED Keel reading: say what her owned figure is for (a co-sponsor sizing its grant), never that it satisfies Taiwanese rules.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d aha candidate but an UNVERIFIED Keel reading; drop 'one-for-one' and 'no risk' (SKELETON 3d: no match claim; budget cuts, row 13; the exchange rate; eligible costs); NT$3.11m is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 and 3e; 22 trading days from 1 Dec 2027 is about twice ILPA's 10-business-day floor for a capital call: a month is generous by practice.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 store; ILPA pairs a hard notice with soft quarterly projections, the two speeds of Q15's draft row (a quarterly 2027 look, then the December confirmation).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e; the 100%-of-unfunded point is good, but fix the critique: the order runs for any amount while the payments' standard holds only down to a 74.5% cut (NUMBERS 5), never 'absorbs any size'.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 store; a confirmation can be 'at least $X'; $76,565 matches NUMBERS 5(c); never state a confirmed amount to co-sponsors before it is owned.

Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 store; 88 days and 62 trading days check (Keel arithmetic); say 'no payment falls due before January 2033', never 'no payment rests on the money', since the payments' standard rests on the extra Treasuries.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; 'Laura's only cost is a plan with no floor, VT or range' is false: a missed deposit also leaves the ten $57,455 short at 0% and $2,287 of the ladder unbought (NUMBERS 5).
Mon 16 Nov: 3a store; no partners cover a gap, the plan's order does; $38,282, $2,388, $35,894 and $2,287 match NUMBERS.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (2); for an individual the default rate is higher and unpublished, so the deposit stays an assumption (Q37-016), never a base rate.

Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 8 (open capital-call defaults are rare); a lender-side source.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (2); the likely bad case is a smaller deposit, which runs the same order, and 'most' holds to a 49.0% cut (NUMBERS 5); a 2009 forecast for institutions.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; practice notice periods conflict (about 10 to 30 days); ILPA's written standard is row 1.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; no systematic data on investor defaults exist, so the deposit is stated as an assumption, not a probability; a theory paper.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 16 (a month-before reminder and a three-months-late escalation).
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 16 (a 30-60-90 day ladder with 90 days as the decision point); the 2014 policy's issuer is unconfirmed.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1; a gift office reviews pledges on 1 December and considers write-off at 90 days overdue: practice lands on the table's own two marks.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 and 3e; silence keeps the file open, so no word by 1 December is a question, never a reason (IPS l.17, CANON A34).
Mon 16 Nov: store; write-off clocks run a year or more because universities have many donors; Laura's line is a quarter because what the 2028 money buys waits on it.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 16 (three months late as the escalation point).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d; audited allowances show written gifts lose about 2-15%, a contrast with her owned bottom (a pledge is owed, her floor owned); the percentages are Keel arithmetic.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 20 (pledge allowances of a few percent), from a 2011 self-reported survey.
Mon 16 Nov: store; pledge losses come in lumps, so one promise cannot be averaged; one institution, Keel arithmetic.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 store; pension law presumes the worst when a certificate is missing; a contrast only, never copied as a trigger (CANON A34).
Mon 16 Nov: same structural idea as row 2 (a soft early checkpoint and a hard late one), in pension law.

Mon 16 Nov: store; checked at the card's source 16 Nov: 101(d) is the missed-contribution notice ('before the 60th day'), 101(j) the funding-based limitation notice ('within 30 days'); the card's correction holds.
Mon 16 Nov: store; quarterly instalments are why a big yearly sum is watched in quarters; never an instalment schedule for Laura.
Mon 16 Nov: same principle as row 33 (grace shrinks as the harm nears); the PBGC's 30-day waiver.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; full-year figures come months late, as her late-2027 royalties do (Q12-008); Keel inference.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 store; lenders watch the income stream (household early-warning signs), the reason to watch her 2027 earnings, not only the date.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 and 3e; 31 March 2028 is 90 days after 1 January (leap year), the line ECB supervisors use for a non-performing loan: the cut-off reads as a standard, not a guess.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 store; 31 March is a late indicator by design: it decides and does not warn; the warning is the 2027 look.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; reluctance to respond is an early sign, a reason to look closer, never a trigger (CANON A34).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e, why the two reasons carry different grace: a Treasury default is five business days late because a payment rests on it, the deposit 90 days because its first need is 2033; one indenture.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the OCC's cure yardstick is about a month.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 store; law's checklist for a money notice (amount, date, place, payee, consequence), which row 1 already mostly meets.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; a month confirms money but cannot raise it; never a plan step (the case names earnings and no home); Keel arithmetic.
Mon 16 Nov: same idea as row 36 on a slower, UNVERIFIED secondary measure.

Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 1 store; the counts check (33 days, 22 and 62 trading days) but the NYSE 2027-28 holidays are UNVERIFIED: read them at source, and drop 'a month's word, a quarter's grace' (a slogan flip).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and Table 3; restate on the plan's own standard: it holds down to a 74.5% cut and a missed deposit leaves the ten $57,455 short at 0% (NUMBERS 5), never 98.4% or $3,016 at forward rates (AHA register reserve 5b).

Mon 16 Nov: 3c; a parallel of method only: S&P would not admit the floor fund at all (row 3), so never imply it would value the fund with a haircut; the 0.5% is Caplet's, never S&P's.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.2 and 3a aha: S&P's eligibility line, 'a fixed principal amount due at its maturity', is the line TNA note 2 drew; never call a fund's payout fixed.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a and 2.2 honest limit: no Fitch-rated escrow may hold a fund; that an ETF is a 'mutual fund' here is Keel's reading.
